text.title: bun-runtime Core Rules
text.summary: Nine testable rules for greenfield Bun-based JS/TS services: six on the scaffold itself and three that resolve the decision tree's run, block and skip branches.

rule.statement: Pin the Bun version in package.json `packageManager` field AND in CI via `oven-sh/setup-bun@v2` with explicit `bun-version`. Never use 'latest'.
rule.rationale: Reproducibility requires identical Bun versions across developer machines, CI, and production containers. LLMs default to 'latest' which breaks builds across teams when Bun releases a non-backwards-compatible change.

rule.statement: Define `dev`, `start`, `test`, and `build` scripts in package.json. Use `bun --watch` for dev (full restart), not `bun --hot` (persists state).
rule.rationale: --hot keeps top-level singletons alive across reloads; edited config does not take effect until a full restart. --watch ensures clean module reloads.

rule.statement: Set `frozen-lockfile = true` under `[install]` in bunfig.toml. Enable coverage under `[test]`.
rule.rationale: Frozen lockfile in CI detects lockfile drift (identical semantics to npm ci). Coverage flag avoids ad-hoc instrumentation.

rule.statement: Set `moduleResolution: "bundler"` in tsconfig.json. Required for Bun's native module resolution.
rule.rationale: Bun handles modern resolution natively; 'bundler' mode enables Bun-specific path resolution without ts-node shims.

rule.statement: Use `Bun.serve` (or a framework like Hono on top of it) for HTTP servers. Do not use `node:http` when running on Bun.
rule.rationale: Bun.serve is measurably faster than node:http for I/O-heavy routes due to JavaScriptCore optimisations. The API is web-standard (Request → Response) and edge-compatible.

rule.statement: Use `Bun.file()` for static reads. Lazy-loaded and faster than `fs.readFileSync`.
rule.rationale: Bun.file returns a lazy Blob; data is read only when `.text()`/`.json()`/`.arrayBuffer()` is called.

rule.statement: When every Applies-If holds (Bun-viable JS/TS project, single-binary toolchain wanted, oven-sh/setup-bun@v2 available, team will pin the version) and the four required fields of 02-output-contract.xml can be filled from the repo, the run MUST be started by the trigger event named in Prerequisites (a new service scaffold, or a Node-to-Bun migration ticket) and MUST end in one output record that carries bun_version as an exact X.Y.Z, tsconfig_module_resolution="bundler", bunfig_frozen_lockfile=true, server_uses_bun_serve=true, all four scripts (dev, start, test, build), produced_by="bun-runtime", the owner, and a non-empty evidence list pointing at the commit or PR that introduced package.json, bunfig.toml and the CI workflow. scripts/validate-bun-runtime.py MUST pass on that record before the scaffold is merged.

rationale.source: Bun documentation (bun.sh/docs: bunfig, bun test, Bun.serve); oven-sh/setup-bun README

rule.rationale: The scaffold is five files that drift independently; a record that names the version, the resolution mode, the lockfile flag and the server primitive in one place is what lets a reviewer or a later agent check the repo against the intent without re-deriving it. Tying the run to a named trigger and an evidence commit is what separates a methodology application from a folklore change nobody can trace when Bun ships a breaking release.

rule.statement: When the Applies-If conditions hold but a required field of the output record cannot be filled from the inputs (no Bun version decided for the CI runner, no owner in the team roster, no output target path, or no evidence anchor), the run MUST stop before writing any file: no package.json with packageManager "bun@latest", no bunfig.toml with frozen-lockfile left false, no record with a placeholder such as "TBD" in a required field. The block MUST be recorded as a ticket comment naming the exact Prerequisites row that is missing, and the tree is re-entered only once that artefact exists.

rationale.source: Bun documentation, bun install --frozen-lockfile; JSON Schema 2020-12 (required keywords)

rule.rationale: A partial scaffold is worse than none: a package.json pinned to "latest" passes local builds and fails CI the week Bun bumps a minor, and a bunfig without frozen-lockfile silently re-resolves dependencies on every install (fm-01, fm-05). The output contract makes the four fields required precisely so that the validator can refuse the half-record; naming the missing input turns a vague 'blocked' into a task somebody can close.

rule.statement: When any Applies-If fails or any Skip-If trips (a registry or dependency that Bun cannot install, a Node native module with no Bun shim, no capacity to run Bun beside Node during migration), no bun-runtime record is produced. The skip MUST be written as a one-line decision that names the failing condition with its evidence (the registry URL, the module name and the bun install or runtime error, or the capacity decision and who made it) and routes the task to a Related methodology whose preconditions do hold, such as best-practices-2026 for the Node-based baseline. A skip without a named condition and evidence is treated as unresolved, not as a decision.

rationale.source: Bun documentation, Node.js compatibility and Node-API status pages

rule.rationale: Bun's Node compatibility is version-dependent, so 'Bun does not work for us' recorded without the module name or error is unfalsifiable and gets re-litigated every quarter; anchoring the skip to the concrete blocker lets the team re-check it against the compatibility page for the next release and lets the routed methodology inherit the finding instead of rediscovering it.
